title: Prime-localized transition base changes
statement: Let Λ be a preorder, A→B ring diagrams and D a diagram of B_i-modules. Let q_i be primes of B_i, contracting compatibly along every transition [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Suppose A^l,B^l,D^l are diagrams with B^l_i-module structures, base-to-top maps φ_i, natural stage maps ρA_i,ρB_i commuting with the base-to-top maps, and numerator maps ζ_i commuting with module transitions. Suppose ρA_i presents A^l_i as localization at q_i contracted to A_i, ρB_i presents B^l_i as localization at q_i, and the B_i-linear maps induced by ζ_i (with action restricted through ρB_i) are IsLocalizedModule at q_i [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Suppose localized module transitions are semilinear. If the original canonical ring base changes B_i tensor over A_i A_j→B_j and module base changes B_j tensor over B_i D_i→D_j are isomorphisms with their pure-tensor formulas [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], then every localized ring transition map B^l_i tensor over A^l_i A^l_j→B^l_j presents B^l_j as a localization at a submonoid and takes b tensor a to B^l(f)(b)φ_j(a). Every localized module base change B^l_j tensor over B^l_i D^l_i is B^l_j-linearly equivalent to D^l_j, taking b tensor x to bD^l(f)(x). No colimit, finiteness, Noetherianity or local-hom hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Fix a transition f. Localization ring-hom extensionality on A_i localized proves B^l(f) composed with phi_i equals phi_j composed with A^l(f): precomposition with rhoA_i reduces this to eta naturality and the three supplied commuting squares. The tensor universal property (Algebra.TensorProduct.lift) constructs t with the required pure-tensor formula. The heterobasic tensor map k induced by rhoA_i, rhoB_i, rhoA_j and the inverse of the supplied ring equivalence give u:B_j -> T, where T=B^l_i tensor over A^l_i A^l_j. Tensor induction and the pure-tensor formula prove t composed with u equals rhoB_j. They also prove u(B(f)(b))=rhoB_i(b) tensor 1 and u(eta_j(a))=1 tensor rhoA_j(a).

Set W=t^{-1}(units of B^l_j) and L=Localization W. The map psi=(T -> L) composed with u sends every element of B_j outside q_j to a unit: its u-image belongs to W because t(u(c))=rhoB_j(c) is a unit. IsLocalization.lift extends psi uniquely to psi_l:B^l_j -> L. Show psi_l composed with t equals T -> L by tensor ring-hom extensionality, then localization ring-hom extensionality on each factor. On denominator-one elements these two equalities reduce respectively to the rhoB naturality square and the eta square, followed by the two formulas for u from the previous step. Lift t to v:L -> B^l_j since t sends W to units. Localization ring-hom extensionality on rhoB_j proves v composed with psi_l is the identity, using t composed with u=rhoB_j. Localization ring-hom extensionality on T -> L proves psi_l composed with v is the identity, using psi_l composed with t=T -> L. Bundle these explicitly constructed inverse maps into a T-algebra equivalence. IsLocalization.isLocalization_of_algEquiv transports the canonical localization witness from L to B^l_j.

For the module conclusion, restrict scalars through the commuting rhoB square and install its scalar towers. Extract the two supplied linear localization maps ell_i and ell_j; IsLocalizedModule.isBaseChange makes them base-change maps to B^l_i and B^l_j. The supplied original equivalence gives the B_i-linear map d:x -> e(1 tensor x), whose value is D(f)(x), and IsBaseChange.of_equiv proves it is base change to B_j. Semilinearity makes d_l=D^l(f) a B^l_i-linear map to D^l_j with scalars restricted through B^l(f). Numerator naturality proves d_l composed with ell_i equals ell_j composed with d. IsBaseChange.comp on d and ell_j identifies the latter composite as base change to B^l_j. IsBaseChange.of_comp cancels ell_i from this equality and proves that d_l is base change to B^l_j. Its IsBaseChange.equiv is the required linear equivalence; IsBaseChange.equiv_tmul gives the stated formula for every localized x directly, with no separate denominator-clearing step.
